stories.title: Canada to Retaliate with Equal Tariffs Following US Trade Dispute
stories.summary: After failing to reach a trade agreement, the United States has imposed 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian goods. In response, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that Canada will match these tariffs 'dollar for dollar' to protect its workers and businesses. The trade tensions mark a significant escalation in relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Fatal Sword Attack at Swedish School Leaves One Dead and Three Injured
stories.summary: A sword attack at a high school in Fagersta, central Sweden, resulted in one death and three injuries. The victim was a 17-year-old girl. An 18-year-old male suspect has been arrested following the incident, which occurred as schools reopened in the area. Police are investigating potential online influences that may have incited the attack.

stories.title: Russian Drone Strikes on Shopping Mall in Kryvyi Rih Kill 15 to 16 People
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes targeted a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, resulting in the deaths of at least 15 to 16 people and injuring over 130 others. The attack was described as a 'double-tap' strike, where a second wave of drones hit the area shortly after the initial strike, reportedly targeting emergency responders. Zelenskyy condemned the assault as an act of barbarism.

stories.title: Supreme Court Temporarily Allows Construction of $400 Million White House Ballroom
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court has granted a temporary order allowing the continuation of construction on a $400 million ballroom at the White House, a project associated with President Donald Trump. This decision comes after lower courts had previously ordered a halt to the work, citing the need for congressional approval. The ruling provides a temporary victory for the Trump administration as it navigates ongoing legal challenges regarding the renovation.

stories.title: TikTok to Pay $400 Million in Landmark Children's Privacy Settlement
stories.summary: TikTok has agreed to a $400 million settlement with the US Department of Justice following allegations that it violated children's online privacy laws. The lawsuit, filed in 2024, accused TikTok and its parent company ByteDance of collecting extensive data from users under the age of 13 without parental consent. The settlement is considered one of the largest of its kind in the United States.

stories.title: Trump Campaigns for Darline Graham in South Carolina Ahead of GOP Runoff
stories.summary: President Donald Trump held a rally in South Carolina to support Sen. Darline Graham, who is running in a Republican runoff to replace her late brother, Lindsey Graham. During the event, Trump addressed a protester who interrupted his speech, humorously stating that the heckler's mother would be voting for him. The runoff is set for next week, and Trump urged Republicans to rally behind Graham as the midterm elections approach.

stories.title: Pentagon Dismisses Leadership of Stars and Stripes Amid Editorial Independence Concerns
stories.summary: The Pentagon has dismissed the editor-in-chief, publisher, and a reporter of Stars and Stripes, citing insubordination. The firings occurred after the editor and reporter publicly opposed potential editorial interference from the Defense Department. This action raises concerns about the independence of the military news outlet, which has a history of editorial autonomy.

stories.title: Ebola Outbreak in DRC Surges Exponentially, Death Toll Exceeds 2,500
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating rapidly, with the United Nations reporting that the death toll has surpassed 2,500. This outbreak is now considered the deadliest in the country's history, spreading at a rate 18 times faster than previous records. Health officials are warning that existing funding to combat the outbreak may soon run out.

stories.title: Australia Takes 101-Run Lead Against Bangladesh in Second Test
stories.summary: In the second Test match against Bangladesh, Australia established a 101-run lead after bowling Bangladesh out for just 64 runs in their first innings. The match saw a total of 18 wickets fall on the first day, with Australia's left-arm bowlers playing a crucial role in the wicket-taking spree. Australia ended the day at 50 for 3 in their second innings.

stories.title: Trial Begins for Tupac Shakur's Murder, Accused Claims Nephew Fired Fatal Shots
stories.summary: The trial regarding the murder of rapper Tupac Shakur has commenced in Las Vegas, years after his death. Duane Davis, 63, is accused of orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed Shakur in 1996. In a recorded police interview from 2008, Davis stated that his nephew, Orlando Anderson, fired the shots that killed the hip-hop star.

A forensic psychiatrist testified about these effects during the proceedings.

stories.title: Escalating Violence in West Bank Amid Settler Blockades and Attacks
stories.summary: Violence in the occupied West Bank is intensifying, particularly in areas designated for a future Palestinian state. A Palestinian-American has returned to his village of Qusra to protect it from increasing settler attacks, which have surged amid ongoing settlement expansion. Reports indicate that violent incidents involving Israeli settlers in Palestinian-controlled areas have nearly doubled since 2025, as settlers pursue aggressive expansion efforts.
